mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the 5-year moving average coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-period SMA by at least 0.25 percentage points within the same month.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) when the trigger occurs, or the 5-period SMA does not exist due to insufficient history.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to market anticipation of tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0 and remains above 3.0 for at least two consecutive months.
failure_condition: During the same 60-day window, the 60-day forward return is positive in at least 70% of high-inflation periods (rolling 12-month comparison).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST industrial production exceeding the prior month's 10% threshold is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals accelerating economic demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 10% relative to the previous month.
failure_condition: Across 10 such monthly spikes, the average 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in PAYEMS employment months before a 20-day S&P 500 forward return suggests labor market strength that supports corporate optimism and equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month compared to the prior month.
failure_condition: In 5 such labor strength months, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of cases (rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in INDPRO for three months indicates weakening manufacturing capacity, which predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates profit compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months.
failure_condition: During three such contraction periods, the 60-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases in both HOUST and RSAFS above their respective 5-period moving averages indicate dual demand drivers and are associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: Both HOUST > HOUST_5MA and RSAFS > RSAFS_5MA in the same month.
failure_condition: Across 10 such interaction months, the 20-day forward return is not positive in more than 70% of cases (rolling t-test).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.0% for two consecutive months during a non-recession regime, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as lower unemployment supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.0% for two consecutive months and is above 2.5% in the prior month.
failure_condition: In 5 such episodes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months in a non-inflationary regime predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases for three consecutive months and remains below its 12-month low.
failure_condition: During four such three-month declines, the 5-day forward return is not negative in more than 80% of cases (rolling window).
